name: Broccoli
grown_as: Calabrese: one large green head cut in summer and autumn, then smaller side shoots. William's records list a green calabrese and 'Cezar'.
habit: An upright plant 60 to 90 cm on a thick stem, the leaves round a single domed head of green flower buds 10 to 20 cm across at the top; side shoots follow from the leaf joints. Flowers the same year if not cut.

leaf.arrangement: Alternate, spiralling up the thick stem
leaf.type: Simple, often with a few small lobes on the lower part of the blade (lyre-shaped)
leaf.outline: Long and oblong to obovate, 30 to 50 cm, with one to three pairs of small lobes near the base
leaf.base: Narrowing into a long stalk, the small lobes running down it
leaf.margin: Wavy, irregularly scalloped and slightly frilled, no sharp teeth
leaf.veins: A thick pale midrib and strong pale side veins
leaf.surface: Hairless, with a waxy grey bloom

flower.form: A cross-shaped flower of four petals
flower.petals: Four, free, broad and rounded with a long narrow claw, spreading flat
flower.centre: Six stamens, four long and two short, with yellow anthers, round a green style
flower.behind: Four narrow upright green sepals hugging the petal claws
flower.carried: In long, loose spikes on a tall branched stem; the closed buds stay above the open flowers at the top of each spike

fruit: Long, slender pods 5 to 10 cm, cylindrical with slight bumps over the seeds, ending in a short beak 0.5 to 1 cm, spreading upwards along the stems. Green, drying straw-brown and splitting from the bottom to show a pale papery partition. Seeds round, 2 mm, dark red-brown to grey-black.
seedling: Two kidney-shaped seed leaves on short stalks, broader than long with a notch at the tip, like a heart with the stalk at its point, waxy grey-green; the first true leaves oval to round on long stalks, waxy blue-green with wavy edges.
winter: Nothing: grown as an annual and cleared by winter.

leaf: a long blade with wavy, scalloped edges and small lobes near the base
a long thick pale stalk and midrib
bloom: four pale yellow rounded petals in a cross
narrow upright sepals hugging the claws
closed buds above the open flowers
seed: round dark red-brown to grey-black seed 2 mm
seedling: two kidney-shaped seed leaves notched at the tip
young: an upright plant of long-stalked waxy blue-green leaves
crop: one large domed head of tightly packed green flower buds on a thick stem
the buds tiny and grainy, not a smooth curd
flower: the head opened out into branching stems
seedhead: long slender pods with short beaks along tall stems

look_alikes: Cauliflower has a white curd, not separate buds. Sprouting broccoli makes many small loose spears, usually purple. All the cabbage-family crops (cabbage, cauliflower, broccoli, sprouts, kale) are one species and share the waxy blue-green leaf; they differ in what is eaten. Swede and oilseed rape have bluish clasping stem leaves but their young leaves are hairy. Turnip and pak choi (Brassica rapa) have bright yellow flowers held above their buds.
